$comment: The source of sf-alert's element plumbing (core/js/element-manifest.js). Taken from simai/ui-control control/smart-architecture/migration/out/alert (migration/convert-1.3.8.mjs over simai/ui-source@5100227); standard simai.smart-component 1.3.8, vocabulary 1.1.5. Every x-todo of the conversion is decided: x-decisions says how.

status.summary: What the alert reports, in the shared status vocabulary. The words this component used before — clear and danger — are still accepted and mean neutral and error.

appearance.summary: How the alert looks, one of the three notice looks (owner decision C110): default the border and the status fill, outlined the border only, flat the status fill without a border, lifted by the card's shadow.

icon.summary: Optional icon override. Use none to hide the semantic icon.

supporting-text.summary: Supporting body text at the normal text size.

action-text.summary: Visible label of the primary optional action.

action.summary: Stable action value emitted in sf-alert-action.

secondary-action-text.summary: Visible label of the secondary optional action.

secondary-action.summary: Stable secondary action value emitted in sf-alert-action.

actions-layout.summary: Where the actions stand: auto puts them in the row with the text while the alert is wide enough and under the text when narrower (layout L3a); under keeps them under the text at every width, for a long text. Any other word is auto.

closable.summary: Render an explicitly named close action.

close-label.summary: Localized accessible name of the close action. Empty: the text of the page's language ("Close alert" in English).

action.summary: The trigger's data-action or data-alert-action value; empty when neither is set.
An action button ([data-action] or [data-alert-action]) inside the alert was activated. Bubbles and is composed; not cancelable. The alert stays.

close.summary: The alert is being dismissed by its close button or dismiss()/close(). Bubbles and is composed; not cancelable; the element is removed after it.

close.x-summary: Dismisses the alert with reason api: sends the cancelable request close first; a page that prevents it keeps the alert
close.summary: Alias of dismiss(): dispatches sf-alert-close and removes the alert after its exit transition. Returns the element.

supporting-text.x-summary: The supporting text with markup, in place of the supporting-text setting: a help link at its end (owner decision C126, «Узнать больше»). Text and a link only; an action is a button (action-text, secondary-action-text).

default.$comment: The Lit template in JavaScript, the migration form of §5.2 (§16).

accessibility.$comment: The root is a live region (§4.8, §7.4.1): role status (polite) for neutral, info and success, role alert (assertive) for warning and error -- for an alert put in the page after its load event. An alert printed with the page (in it at the load, or carrying its server-printed first paint) is role status at every level: it is not news and must not interrupt (NS-1). The host's own role attribute, status or alert, is the author's choice and always wins (§3.1, as on sf-toast). Its name is the heading, else the host's aria-label. Tab reaches its action and close buttons.

aliases.$comment: Dated aliases of sf-alert for the shim (core/js/aliases.js, standard §16 item 20). mode: same-detail (the shim sends the new and the old name), detail-adds (the new detail holds the old fields), attribute-and-property, host-attribute (no shim), manifest-only (the DOM name does not change), retired (no new name; kept and noted by the component until the date).

rows.summary: Legacy name for status, still honoured. See contracts/public-api-axes.json.
Legacy name for appearance, still honoured. See contracts/public-api-axes.json.

rows.note: the DOM name stays; detail keeps action and loses the element alert
rows.summary: An action button ([data-action] or [data-alert-action]) inside the alert was activated. Bubbles and is composed; not cancelable. The alert stays.

rows.note: the DOM name stays and is cancelable now; detail is {reason}, without the element alert
rows.summary: The alert is being dismissed by its close button or dismiss()/close(). Bubbles and is composed; not cancelable; the element is removed after it.

x-summary: Persistent inline notice with semantic roles, optional actions and dismiss behavior.
x-renamed: settings.title → heading: "title" is a property of HTMLElement.prototype (§3.1, §16 item 26), alias dated
events.action: 1 carried field(s) held the element, not data (§8)
events.sf-alert-action → action (the DOM name without sf-<tag>-)
events.close: 1 carried field(s) held the element, not data (§8)
events.sf-alert-close → close (the DOM name without sf-<tag>-)
settings.type → status, settings.variant → appearance: the axes' old names, dated setting aliases
actions.dismiss → close: one action for one act, a dated action alias
x-decisions: own-verb-words: action is a verb of the alert alone (the person pressed one of its two action buttons; detail.action names which); its word is lang events.action.label. It is a report, not a request the alert waits on, so it is not cancelable.
version: 1.0.0 → 1.1.0: title, type, variant and dismiss are dated aliases, close becomes a cancelable request with a reason; a minor while the aliases hold (§4.10).

a11y-role: one live region on the root (§4.8, §7.4.1): status (polite) for neutral, info and success, alert (assertive) for warning and error, written with when on status. The name is the heading, else the host's aria-label (§3.1). Since 1.2.2 (NS-1) the level's role is for an alert put in the page after its load; one printed with the page is status, and a host role of status or alert wins.

events: close is the request the alert sends before it leaves (cancelable, reason close from its own button or api from close()); a page that prevents it keeps the alert and close() answers refused. The detail carries data only (§8): the element alert leaves it.

x-target text, tone and press (stand 24's record panel note): not added. text and tone would be second names of supporting-text and status, which §4 does not give one setting; a rule binds settings.supporting-text and writes status. press is the alert's action event (action), not a press of the alert.
template: templates.default names the Lit template js/templates/default.js, the migration form §5.2 allows.
examples: examples.json from studio.fixture.json and studio.scenario.json plus the statuses and both actions; probe.json drives the close and action buttons, the refused close and the aliases.
skeleton: none; the alert has no port and no late data: its static markup is its first paint (§5.4).
css-variables: the eight public variables the alert sheet already reads (src/core/contracts/public-variables.v1.json).

version 1.1.1: the first-paint snapshots are retaken: the JSON island is printed once (no held copy), the icon font's state (sf-icon loaded, sf-icon-loaded) is left out, a closed surface prints closed and a size or place the code measured (a non-zero px width, height, inset, clip or transform) is left out, so a snapshot is the same on every run.
version 1.1.2: the first-paint sheet list names the utility sheets its templates draw with (core.runtime 1.0.7 asks for them before the element draws: the style gate).

version 1.1.3: the bundle carries no element layer of its own -- element-manifest, aliases, the alias table, the host port, deprecations, page actions, the layer stack, the open-surface mark and the instance path come from the page's shared runtime (SF.runtimeModule, runtime ABI 1, core.runtime 1.1.0), one instance per page -- and embeds of this file only the keys the runtime reads. Behaviour unchanged.
version 1.1.8: the outcomes applied and refused come from core/js/element-manifest.js (core.runtime 1.25.0, duplication audit A-26) instead of a copy of its own; behaviour unchanged.

version 1.1.10 (one number above the two unreleased 1.1.9 it joins; its first-paint sheet list follows the merged buttons): the sf-button and sf-button-icon it draws are asked for their current names (appearance ghost for link, status danger for error; actions block, decisions C13 and C15), so the template uses no dated alias; nothing it draws changes.
version 1.1.11: the first-paint snapshot is retaken: a nested sized component now carries data-sf-size-relative at first paint (density C22, core.runtime 1.45.0); nothing it draws changes.

version 1.2.0: the notice's geometry and actions, the toast's numbers (decision C35; DEV acceptance D3 extends it to every notice). The actions are unsized low buttons (32, compact and phone 28) whose label is the notice's text size, the first tonal primary and the second ghost on-surface (before: size 1/2 filled and outline on-surface); the close is sf-button-icon kind close height low (32 / 28 / 28, before 40 / 32 / 36), centred on the first line; title to text 0 (before 12 / 8), text to actions --sf-space-1/2 (before --sf-space-1), padding and icon gap as the toast (component.alerts 1.1.0).

version 1.2.1 (2026-11-11, CB-01, decision C15): the second action writes sf-button--ghost beside sf-button--link, its former name (journal class-button-link-to-ghost, until 2027-01-01). Nothing is drawn differently. Settings, values, events and keys unchanged.

version 1.2.2 (2026-11-12, NS-1 of the notices study; with C110 variant E): an alert printed with the page -- in it at the load event, or carrying its server-printed first paint -- is role status at every level, so a warning or an error already on the page is not announced as an interruption. An alert put in the page after the load, or put back after it was taken out, keeps its level's role (alert for warning and error). The host's role attribute, status or alert, is the author's explicit choice and wins (as on sf-toast). Settings, values, events and keys unchanged.

version 1.3.0 (2026-11-13, owner decisions C114 and C115; component.alerts 1.2.0): a minor. The job is the state of this page or section (C114 (1)); the docs name its neighbours (sf-alert-bar the whole product, sf-toast a short reply to an action, the notification centre the history, sf-confirm a decision). Where the actions stand is layout L3a (C115): in the row with the text from 36rem of the alert's own width with one action and from 48rem with two (a size container query on the alert, the step its whole width), centred on the text block, the label on the title line with a one-line text; narrower, under the text from its start. Under the text, the bottom inset is even with the top (C114 (5), NS-9). The callout is a recipe of this element (C114 (7)): status info, appearance outlined, no close, no actions. Events and keys unchanged. A new setting actions-layout (owner 2026-11-13, #q-layout-override): auto (the default) is L3a, under keeps the actions under the text at every width with the same gap and the even bottom (a long text in the row is taller than under it, 174 against 146 at 800); the template adds the class form sf-alert--actions-under; any other word is auto, as every enum setting; no alias.

version 1.3.1 (2026-11-13, owner decision C126; component.alerts 1.2.1): a patch. A link in the alert's text is help only («Узнать больше»), every action a button; the link is the text's own ink (on-surface, or on-<status>-container on a status container), not the theme's link blue, underlined at the link weight, the line doubled under the pointer, its keyboard ring the same ink -- 4.5:1 and more for the link and 3:1 and more for the ring on every status and look, light and dark (the sheet, core mix/_mix__notice-link.scss shared with sf-toast and sf-alert-bar). The supporting-text slot the template already read is declared, and the example help-link shows it. No saturated look: the three looks stay, the action stays tonal surface (C110 E). Settings, values, events and keys unchanged.

version 1.4.0 (2026-11-13, owner decision C110 as amended 2026-11-12, look (в); component.alerts 1.3.0): a minor. The three notice looks are the three appearances: outlined (а) the border only, default (б) the border and the status fill, flat (в) the status fill without a border, now with the card's shadow (--sf-shadow-raised, the raised place of the four shadow places); only flat casts a shadow. New example flat-shadow. Settings, values, events and keys unchanged.

version 1.4.1 (2026-11-13, owner decision C105 H4/H6, spacing audit A1; component.alerts 1.3.1): a patch. The 1 px border stands inside the inline inset, as the fields' C77 inset: the padding is --sf-space-1 less the border, so the status icon, the letters and the cross stand 16 from the outer edge (compact and phone 12), not 17 (13). The action thresholds of C115 stay the whole width (36rem and 48rem). Settings, values, events and keys unchanged.

live_region_guidance.assertive: role=alert only for a newly inserted urgent message
live_region_guidance.polite: role=status for a newly inserted non-urgent update
live_region_guidance.static: omit a live-region role when the notice is present on initial page load

ai_guidance.use_when: Use sf-alert for persistent inline guidance, warning, error or success feedback inside the page flow.
do_not: Do not use Alert for transient overlay feedback; use Toast
Do not choose a semantic type only for its color
Do not add role=alert to a static message that is already present on page load
Do not copy generated ui-smart code
Do not move host data or access decisions into the component
ai_guidance.minimal_example: <sf-alert status="info" title="Update available" supporting-text="Save your changes before refreshing."></sf-alert>

accessibility.focus: Actions use native focus-visible behavior; after dismissal the application restores focus only when it was inside the removed notice.

onAction.summary: Adds a listener for sf-alert-action; the handler receives (action, detail, event). Returns the element.

onClose.summary: Adds a listener for sf-alert-close; the handler receives (detail, event). Returns the element.

dismiss.summary: Dispatches sf-alert-close, then removes the alert from the DOM after its exit transition (at once under reduced motion). Returns the element.
